results.name: The Rise of LLMJacking: How Threat Actors Monetize Compromised Cloud and Model Resources
results.description: Threat actors are hijacking enterprise access to Large Language Models through a tactic called LLMJacking, impacting organizations across North America, South America, and Asia Pacific in financial services, retail, technology, and transportation sectors. Unlike cryptojacking's gradual consumption, LLMJacking generates massive spikes in fraudulent cloud charges, with incidents exceeding $100,000 USD daily and reaching $1 million USD cumulatively. Actors establish initial access through exposed cloud identity tokens, IAM credentials, Service Account keys, and stolen API keys. They escalate privileges, conduct reconnaissance, and monetize compromised resources through LLM Mixers—illicit routing gateways that proxy and resell unauthorized LLM access. The ecosystem shows sophisticated specialization with distinct operational clusters coordinating compromises and downstream monetization infrastructure.

results.name: DarkBlinders: Active Espionage Campaign
results.description: A sophisticated cyberespionage operation targeting Israel and the Kurdistan Region of Iraq was conducted by DarkBlinders, the threat actor behind the Blinder Tunnel campaign. Active between August and October 2026, the campaign compromised a high-profile Israeli individual associated with the security sector and a government cloud environment in the Kurdistan Region. The operation employed government webmail, cloud-drive, and meeting-service lures, including phishing infrastructure impersonating the Gulf Cooperation Council Secretariat General and Kuwait's Ministry of Foreign Affairs. GitHub repositories under the PeakyBlindersTeam account served as command-and-control infrastructure. The attackers used selective activation, reviewing metadata from infected hosts before deploying a second-stage backdoor enabling PowerShell command execution. results.name: Exploitation Targeting Node-RED, a Tool Embedded in ICS Products
results.description: On October 30, 2026, exploitation activity was detected targeting CVE-2026-58115, an unauthenticated Node-RED admin API vulnerability. Attackers deployed malicious flows that automatically download and execute Linux bots through three layers of encoding. The exploit originated from IP 4.201.105.116 in Microsoft's network and utilized Node-RED's inject and exec nodes to execute commands without authentication. The dropper retrieved binaries from 85.215.73.250:8080, saving them to RAM-backed storage at /dev/shm/.b to avoid disk forensics. Multiple payload variants were observed, including staged shell scripts and persistent webshells. The activity demonstrates opportunistic mass scanning across multiple CVEs rather than targeted operations. Node-RED is embedded in critical infrastructure products including Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 devices, making this vulnerability particularly significant for industrial control systems environments.

results.name: BITTER Expands Its Arsenal with PapRAT
results.description: A cyberespionage group known as BITTER has been conducting campaigns targeting South Asian organizations using PowerShell scripts and a custom remote access trojan called PapRAT. Three distinct infection chains have been identified: one exploiting Windows ftp.exe with malicious LNK files, another using VHDX disk images containing MSI installers, and a third combining URL shortcuts with WebDAV to deploy PapRAT. The malware exists in both C++ and Rust implementations, with capabilities including command execution, file manipulation, directory enumeration, screenshot capture, and secondary payload delivery. PapRAT maintains persistent access through scheduled tasks and communicates with command-and-control servers over HTTP. The Rust variant introduces enhanced functionality including PowerShell execution and sleep commands. Targets are concentrated in South Asian government, energy, and engineering sectors.

results.name: The Internals of a Badbox Operation
results.description: Investigation reveals a massive supply chain compromise involving MECOOL Android set-top boxes manufactured by Videostrong Technology Co., Ltd. Over 1.3 million devices were pre-infected with the x.cpe backdoor, granting operators system-level access through MQTT infrastructure. The backdoor deploys multiple payloads including residential proxy SDKs and ad fraud modules like AdMoyu, Appsalt, APSolo, LinkFog, and Gaganode. Approximately 500,000 devices remain actively online, predominantly affecting Malaysia, Mexico, and Brazil. The operation functions as a pay-per-install campaign fueling ad fraud and proxy ecosystems. Google has permanently banned Videostrong from the Android ecosystem following these findings. Investigation conducted in partnership with Motion Picture Association, Google, Plume, Trend Micro, Lumen, and HUMAN Security.

results.name: SEO Poisoning Campaign Targets DeepSeek Users: Chinese Threat Actor Deploys Kong RAT via Multi-Stage Attacks
results.description: A sophisticated SEO poisoning campaign targets users searching for DeepSeek AI tools through malicious lookalike domains positioned on first-page search results. The attack employs a multi-stage infection chain beginning with weaponized MSI files disguised as legitimate DeepSeek software. The execution flow progresses through multiple stages involving shellcode, DLL side-loading via legitimate Cyglaunch software, and ultimately deploys Kong RAT. The threat actor registered domains mimicking DeepSeek and distributed ZIP archives containing code-signed fake installers to add legitimacy. Attribution points to a potential Chinese threat actor based on PDB paths referencing '52pojie', a Chinese cybersecurity forum. This campaign appears to be a continuation of previous operations from April 2026 targeting users of Chinese developer tools including FinalShell SSH client, Xshell, and Clash proxy. The final payload includes keylogger functionality and establishes persistence through registry modifications.

results.name: Shutting the Door on the XCPE Botnet
results.description: Google and industry partners dismantled the XCPE backdoor that enrolled over 1.3 million set-top boxes into a botnet. The backdoor was intentionally developed and operated by Videostrong Technology Co., an Android OEM/ODM, who monetized it by selling access to criminal affiliates. These affiliates loaded malware modules conducting ad-fraud, enrolling devices into residential proxy networks, and installing additional malware. The disruption also severed access to at least 10 million additional compromised devices by taking down affiliate C2 domains. The malicious software was built directly into various device models over multiple years with dedicated infrastructure. Google has banned Videostrong from making certified Android devices and implemented improvements to firmware integrity reviews on Android TV devices.

results.name: Hackers Use Fake ChatGPT Plus Billing Emails to Steal Credit Card Details and OTP Codes
results.description: A sophisticated phishing campaign impersonates OpenAI by sending fraudulent ChatGPT Plus billing emails claiming failed subscription payments. Victims are directed to fake payment pages hosted on compromised WordPress instances under Nexcess's nxcli.io infrastructure. The operation features live attacker involvement, where operators monitor submitted credit card information and dynamically decide whether to request one-time passwords through a real-time polling mechanism. After victims submit payment details including card numbers, expiry dates, CVV codes, and cardholder names, the page maintains a loading animation while the browser polls a backend system approximately every 500 milliseconds. The attackers can then redirect victims to verification-code collection pages to complete fraudulent transactions. The campaign uses distinctive redirect domains and identical client-side code across multiple instances.

results.name: CyberStrikeAI attacks educational institutions
results.description: An open-source framework called CyberStrikeAI was used in real-world attacks against educational institutions across Africa and Latin America. The framework combines LLM-based orchestration with a traditional C2 server, where an AI model on the server plans actions and generates commands while an implant executes them on compromised hosts. Attackers initially gained access through compromised SQL Server infrastructure, then deployed the CyberStrikeAI agent which performed reconnaissance, privilege escalation, credential dumping, lateral movement, and data exfiltration. The AI orchestrator automated post-exploitation activities that traditionally require manual operator intervention, reducing the skill barrier for attackers. While the AI component operates server-side, the actual malicious activities on victim systems use standard techniques like Kerberoasting, AS-REP Roasting, LSASS dumps, DCSync, and Golden Ticket attacks, making them detectable through conventional security controls. results.name: VAPOR PANDA Uses AI-Driven ARTEX to Grow Global Espionage Campaign
results.description: VAPOR PANDA conducted a sophisticated espionage campaign beginning October 17, 2026, using the ARTEX AI-driven framework alongside DeepSeek and commercial LLMs to orchestrate parallel intrusions against over 200 organizations worldwide. Targets included foreign ministries across Latin America, Europe, Asia, and the Middle East, plus U.S.-based semiconductor, defense, pharmaceutical, nuclear, and telecommunications entities. The adversary deployed BLOODALCHEMY backdoor, conducted credential spraying, and explicitly instructed AI agents to identify systems without endpoint security sensors. This represents an escalation from single intrusions to multiple simultaneous engagements, with agents autonomously pursuing attack paths while human operators provided strategic direction in Chinese. The campaign demonstrated how threat actors combine open-source AI frameworks with commercial LLMs to dramatically scale intrusion operations beyond manual capabilities.
